name: quadrilateral
title: Quadrilateral
tagline: Quadrilateral from four vertices with derived sides, angles, right angles and an optional splitting diagonal for two-triangle Pythagoras figures; occludable/highlightable.
description: A single simple (convex) quadrilateral drawn from four ordered vertices, with any of its side lengths, interior angles, equal-side ticks and right angles marked, plus an optional drawn diagonal that splits it into two triangles. One figure for rectangles and squares (with a diagonal), right-angled trapeziums, and the general "split it with a diagonal into two right-angled triangles" Pythagoras figures. You place the four vertices as a sketch in any units, in order around the perimeter; the model derives every side length, interior angle and diagonal length from them and auto-fits the figure, so the marks stay correct. The optional diagonal is drawn between two named non-adjacent vertices; its length is derived and can be occluded ("find the diagonal first") or highlighted (the answer). Where the diagonal meets a side at a right angle — the two right triangles of a split figure often have their right angles at different vertices, between the diagonal and a side — mark that right angle on the diagonal entry (diagonals[].angles), not on angles[] (a whole-vertex interior mark would sweep across the diagonal). Interior corner right angles (a rectangle, a right-angled trapezium) are marked on angles[]. Per-element occlusion ("find x"), highlighting, a "not to scale" note and draggable vertices on the web. Override any displayed value with a label for the given data of a not-to-scale exam figure. Place a to-scale sketch and the derived diagonal / fourth side equals the Pythagoras answer, so it can be cross-checked against the boxed value.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the teaching lives on a four-sided figure: a rectangle or square (usually with a diagonal), a right-angled trapezium, a kite, or the general Pythagoras figure where a diagonal splits the quadrilateral into two right-angled triangles. Place four vertices as [x, y] points making a sketch of the quadrilateral, IN ORDER around the perimeter (clockwise or anticlockwise — consecutive vertices must be joined sides); the vertices default to labels A, B, C, D in the order given (override a vertex's label for different names). Reference a side by its two endpoint labels (between: ["A","B"]) and an interior angle by its vertex (at: "A"). The model derives each side length, interior angle and diagonal from the vertices, so for a to-scale figure (e.g. a rectangle placed at [0,0],[12,0],[12,5],[0,5]) just mark the element and the right number shows; for a not-to-scale exam figure place a rough sketch, set notToScale: true, and override each shown value with a label (the given data, e.g. "8 cm", "x"). Common configurations: RECTANGLE / SQUARE with a diagonal — place the four corners to scale, add a diagonals entry (diagonals: [{ between: ["A","C"] }]), mark an interior right angle at a corner if you want the right-triangle explicit, and occlude the diagonal (find AC) or, for a square given its diagonal, label the diagonal and occlude a side. RIGHT-ANGLED TRAPEZIUM — the two right angles are interior corners, so mark them on angles[] ({ at: "A", rightAngle: true }); label the parallel sides and the slant, occlude the unknown side. THE SPLIT FIGURE (two right-angled triangles off one diagonal) — draw the diagonal, then put its right angle(s) on the diagonal: diagonals: [{ between: ["A","C"], angles: [{ at: "C", toward: "B", rightAngle: true }] }] marks the right angle at C between the diagonal CA and the side CB (toward names the adjacent vertex the side reaches). If one triangle's right angle is a genuine corner of the quadrilateral, mark THAT one on angles[] instead. Occlude the diagonal to say "find it first", then occlude the final unknown side and highlight it. Keep the sketch convex and simple (vertices in perimeter order); reflex / self-intersecting quadrilaterals are out of scope in v1. Occlude renders a value as "?"; the element itself stays drawn. EXAM FIGURES with no vertex letters — set vertexLabels: false; the letters stop printing but you still address sides/angles/diagonals by the default A/B/C/D. Mark a right angle with rightAngle: true (a small square instead of an arc + value). Tick equal sides with ticks (1, 2 or 3 — sides with the same count read as equal, as on a kite or square). Cross-block convention: keep the same quadrilateral shape and vertex labels across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track the figure, not a redrawn sketch — change only what is given, occluded or highlighted. A split figure builds up naturally in stages (empty quadrilateral → add the givens → draw the diagonal → solve triangle 1 for the diagonal → solve triangle 2 for the answer). UNITS — set unit: "cm" once per figure to append it to every bare-number length label (derived or authored "12"); a label carrying its own text ("12 cm", "x") stays verbatim. Synonyms a teacher might use: quadrilateral, rectangle, square, oblong, trapezium, trapezoid, right-angled trapezium, kite, parallelogram, four-sided shape, diagonal, diagonal of a rectangle, split into two triangles, drop a perpendicular, Pythagoras, right-angled triangle, hypotenuse, find the diagonal, perimeter of a square from its diagonal, not to scale.

vertices.description: The four corners of the quadrilateral, IN ORDER around the perimeter (clockwise or anticlockwise). Each is a point in any units — place them as a SKETCH of the shape you want; the model derives the side lengths, interior angles and diagonals from them and auto-fits the figure. The order fixes both the sides (consecutive vertices are joined) and the default labels: the first corner is A, the second B, the third C, the fourth D. Keep the shape simple and convex (v1 does not support reflex or self-intersecting quadrilaterals).

at.description: Position of this corner as [x, y] in your own units (y up). Only the SHAPE matters — the figure is scaled to fit.

label.description: Display name for this corner, drawn just outside it. Defaults to A, B, C, D by order. Override for different names (then reference this corner by the new label in sides/angles/diagonals).

sides.description: The sides to LABEL with a length and/or tick as equal. Address each by its two endpoint vertex labels (they must be consecutive corners). The length is DERIVED from the vertices; override with label for the given value or an unknown. Omit a side to leave it bare.

between.description: The two endpoint vertex labels of this side, e.g. ["A","B"] (order does not matter). Must be a genuine side — two consecutive corners.

label.description: Override the displayed length — the given value ("8 cm", "x"). Omit to show the length derived from the vertices.

occlude.description: Render this side's length as "?" — the "find the missing side" hook. The side stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this side (amber) — the answer, or the side in question. Default false.

ticks.description: Draw this many small equal-length ticks across the side. Sides with the SAME tick count read as equal (a square uses 1 on each; a kite pairs sides with 1 and 2). Omit for no tick.

angles.description: The INTERIOR angles to MARK — an arc + value, or a right-angle square. Address each by its vertex label. The measure is DERIVED from the vertices (the angle between the two sides meeting at that corner); override with label. Use rightAngle for a corner right angle (a rectangle, a right-angled trapezium). Omit a vertex to leave its angle unmarked. (For the right angle a DIAGONAL makes with a side, use diagonals[].angles instead — a corner mark would be wrong there.)

at.description: Which corner this angle sits at — the vertex label (e.g. "A").

label.description: Override the displayed value — the given measure on a not-to-scale figure ("110°") or an unknown ("x"). Omit to show the measure derived from the vertices.

occlude.description: Render this angle's value as "?" — the "find the missing angle" hook. The arc still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this angle (amber arc + value). Default false.

bare.description: Mark this angle with the arc ONLY — no value text. Use when the figure marks an angle without giving its size. occlude beats bare. Default false.

rightAngle.description: Mark this corner as a right angle: a small square instead of an arc and value. Use for a rectangle/square corner or the right angles of a right-angled trapezium. Default false.

diagonals.description: Diagonals to DRAW — a straight line between two NON-adjacent corners (e.g. ["A","C"] or ["B","D"]), which splits the quadrilateral into two triangles. The length is DERIVED; occlude it ("find the diagonal first") or highlight it (the answer). A diagonal can carry right-angle / angle marks at its ends where it meets a side (diagonals[].angles) — the split figures' two right triangles usually have their right angles here, at different vertices, between the diagonal and a side. Omit for a plain quadrilateral. At most two.

between.description: The two NON-adjacent corner labels this diagonal joins, e.g. ["A","C"] (order does not matter).

label.description: Override the displayed length of the diagonal — a given value ("8 m") or an unknown ("x"). Omit to leave the diagonal unlabelled unless showLength / occlude is set.

occlude.description: Render the diagonal's length as "?" (the "find the diagonal" hook) and show its length position. The line still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to the diagonal and its length (amber) — the answer, or the diagonal a question is about. Default false.

showLength.description: Show the derived length of the diagonal even with no label. Default false — a bare diagonal draws just the line. (label or occlude also force the length to show.)

angles.description: Angle marks at this diagonal's ends, between the diagonal and one of the sides meeting there — the right angle of a split figure's right triangle. At most one per end. Omit for none.

at.description: Which END of this diagonal the angle sits at — one of the diagonal's two corner labels (e.g. "C").

toward.description: Which side bounds this angle: the adjacent corner that side reaches (e.g. toward "B" marks the angle between the diagonal and the side at→B). Must be a corner adjacent to `at`.

label.description: Override the displayed value — a given measure ("35°") or an unknown ("x°"). Omit to show the measure derived from the sketch.

occlude.description: Render this angle's value as "?". The arc still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this angle (amber). Default false.

bare.description: Arc only, no value text. occlude beats bare. Default false.

rightAngle.description: Mark this as a right angle: a small square between the diagonal and the side, instead of an arc + value. The usual mark for a split figure. Default false.

unit.description: The figure's length unit, e.g. "cm", "m", "mm". Appended to every length label that is a BARE NUMBER — a derived length or a purely numeric authored label ("12" → "12 cm"). A label with any other text ("12 cm", "x", "2x + 1") is shown verbatim — an authored override always wins. Angle labels never take it. Default "" (labels stay bare). Set it once per figure and keep it consistent across a lesson. @2.

vertexLabels.description: Whether to PRINT the vertex letters beside the corners. Set false for exam figures drawn without letters — addressing in sides/angles/diagonals still uses the default A/B/C/D (or custom labels); only the printing is suppressed. Default true.

notToScale.description: Print a "Not to scale" note by the figure. Only when the source figure prints one — most exam figures don't. Default false.

caption.description: An optional line of text centred below the figure — the rule or fact being taught, e.g. "The diagonal of a rectangle splits it into two right-angled triangles". Omit for none.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

draggablePoints.description: Web-only. Let pupils drag a corner to reshape the quadrilateral; the derived side lengths, angles and any diagonal recompute live. Best on a to-scale figure (no overridden labels). Default false.
